fanoutqa_000691.x:
Avatar: The Way of Water :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Following the success of *Avatar* in 2009, two sequels were announced, with the first aiming for a 2014 release. However, the addition of two more sequels—for a total of five films—and the need to develop new technology to film [motion-capture](/wiki/Motion-capture "Motion-capture") scenes underwater, led to significant delays. The filming process, which [occurred simultaneously](/wiki/Back-to-back_film_production "Back-to-back film production") with the third film in the franchise, *[Avatar: Fire and Ash](/wiki/Avatar:_Fire_and_Ash "Avatar: Fire and Ash")*, began in [Manhattan Beach, California](/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California"), on August 15, 2017. Production moved to [Wellington](/wiki/Wellington "Wellington"), New Zealand the following month, and was completed three years later, in September 2020. With an estimated budget of $350–460 million, *Avatar: The Way of Water* is one of the [most expensive](/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_films "List of most expensive films") films ever made. It was produced by Cameron's company [Lightstorm Entertainment](/wiki/Lightstorm_Entertainment "Lightstorm Entertainment").

After repeated delays in release, *Avatar: The Way of Water* premiered at the [Odeon Leicester Square](/wiki/Odeon_Leicester_Square "Odeon Leicester Square") theater in London on December 6, 2022, and was released in the United States on December 16, by [20th Century Studios](/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios"). The film received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised the visual effects and technical achievements but criticized the runtime.[[5]](#cite_note-CNBC-7) It was a major box office success, breaking multiple records. It grossed $2.320 billion in its first theatrical run, becoming the [highest-grossing film of 2022](/wiki/2022_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2022 in film") and the [third-highest-grossing film of all time](/wiki/List_of_highest-gro

*[Alita: Battle Angel](/wiki/Alita:_Battle_Angel "Alita: Battle Angel")* was finally released in 2019, after being in parallel development with *Avatar*. Written by Cameron and friend Jon Landau, the film was directed by [Robert Rodriguez](/wiki/Robert_Rodriguez "Robert Rodriguez") and produced by Cameron.[[105]](#cite_note-105) The film is based on a 1990s Japanese [manga](/wiki/Manga "Manga") series *[Battle Angel Alita](/wiki/Battle_Angel_Alita "Battle Angel Alita"),* depicting a cyborg who cannot remember anything of her past life and tries to uncover the truth. Produced with similar techniques and technology as in *Avatar*, the film starred [Rosa Salazar](/wiki/Rosa_Salazar "Rosa Salazar"), [Christoph Waltz](/wiki/Christoph_Waltz "Christoph Waltz"), [Jennifer Connelly](/wiki/Jennifer_Connelly "Jennifer Connelly"), [Mahershala Ali](/wiki/Mahershala_Ali "Mahershala Ali"), [Ed Skrein](/wiki/Ed_Skrein "Ed Skrein"), [Jackie Earle Haley](/wiki/Jackie_Earle_Haley "Jackie Earle Haley") and [Keean Johnson](/wiki/Keean_Johnson "Keean Johnson"). The film premiered on January 31, 2019, to generally positive reviews and $404 million (equivalent to $487,500,000 in 2024) at the worldwide box office.[[106]](#cite_note-106) In her review, Monica Castillo of *[RogerEbert.com](/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com")* called it "an awe-inspiring jump for [Rodriguez]" and "a visual bonanza", despite the bulky script.[[107]](#cite_note-107) Cameron then returned to the *Terminator* franchise as producer and writer for [Tim Miller](/wiki/Tim_Miller_(director) "Tim Miller (director)")'s *[Terminator: Dark Fate](/wiki/Terminator:_Dark_Fate "Terminator: Dark Fate")* (2019).[[108]](#cite_note-108)

The three [Nordic countries](/wiki/Nordic_countries "Nordic countries") which joined NATO as founding members, Denmark, Iceland and Norway, chose to limit their participation in three areas: there would be no permanent peacetime bases, no nuclear warheads and no Allied military activity (unless invited) permitted on their territory. However, Denmark allowed the US to maintain an existing base, [Thule Air Base (now Pituffik Space Base)](/wiki/Pituffik_Space_Base "Pituffik Space Base"), in Greenland.[[13]](#cite_note-27)

From the mid-1960s to the mid-1990s, [France](/wiki/France "France") pursued a military strategy of independence from NATO under a policy dubbed "Gaullo-Mitterrandism".[[14]](#cite_note-28) [Nicolas Sarkozy](/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy") negotiated the return of France to the integrated military command and the Defence Planning Committee in 2009, the latter being disbanded the following year. France remains the only NATO member outside the [Nuclear Planning Group](/wiki/NATO_Nuclear_Planning_Group "NATO Nuclear Planning Group") and unlike the United States and the United Kingdom, will not commit its nuclear-armed submarines to the alliance.[[15]](#cite_note-29)[[16]](#cite_note-30)

As of March 2024, three additional states have formally informed NATO of their membership aspirations: [Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), [Georgia](/wiki/Georgia_(country) "Georgia (country)"), and [Ukraine](/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine").[[3]](#cite_note-Englargement_five-3)

The **Group of Seven** (**G7**) is an [intergovernmental](/wiki/Intergovernmentalism "Intergovernmentalism") political and economic forum consisting of [Canada](/wiki/Canada "Canada"), [France](/wiki/France "France"), [Germany](/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Japan](/wiki/Japan "Japan"), the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States"); additionally, the [European Union](/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) is a "non-enumerated member". It is organized around shared values of [pluralism](/wiki/Cultural_pluralism "Cultural pluralism"), [liberal democracy](/wiki/Liberal_democracy "Liberal democracy"), and [representative government](/wiki/Representative_democracy "Representative democracy").[[1]](#cite_note-What_is_the_G7-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) G7 members are major [IMF advanced economies](/wiki/Developed_country#IMF_advanced_economies "Developed country").

Originating from an *ad hoc* gathering of [finance ministers](/wiki/Finance_minister "Finance minister") in 1973, the G7 has since become a formal, high-profile venue for discussing and coordinating solutions to major [global issues](/wiki/List_of_global_issues "List of global issues"), especially in the areas of [trade](/wiki/Trade "Trade"), [security](/wiki/Security "Security"), [economics](/wiki/Economy "Economy"), and [climate change](/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change").[[4]](#cite_note-4) Each member's [head of government](/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") or [state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), along with the EU's [Commission president](/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission "President of the European Commission") and [European Council president](/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council"), meet annually at the G7 Summit; other high-ranking officials of the G7 and the EU meet throughout the year. Bernanke was educated at East Elementary, J.V. Martin Junior High, and [Dillon High School](/wiki/Dillon_High_School "Dillon High School"), where he was class [valedictorian](/wiki/Valedictorian "Valedictorian") and played saxophone in the [marching band](/wiki/Marching_band "Marching band").[[26]](#cite_note-26) Since Dillon High School did not offer [calculus](/wiki/Calculus "Calculus") at the time, Bernanke taught it to himself.[[27]](#cite_note-Time09-27)[[28]](#cite_note-28) Bernanke scored 1590 out of 1600 on the [SAT](/wiki/SAT "SAT")[[27]](#cite_note-Time09-27)[[29]](#cite_note-29) and was a [National Merit Scholar](/wiki/National_Merit_Scholarship_Program "National Merit Scholarship Program").[[30]](#cite_note-30) He also was a contestant in the [1965 National Spelling Bee](/wiki/38th_Scripps_National_Spelling_Bee "38th Scripps National Spelling Bee").[[31]](#cite_note-ben-31)[[32]](#cite_note-Greenville65-32)

Bernanke entered [Harvard College](/wiki/Harvard_College "Harvard College") in 1971,[[33]](#cite_note-33) where he lived in [Winthrop House](/wiki/Winthrop_House "Winthrop House"), as did the future chief executive officer of [Goldman Sachs](/wiki/Goldman_Sachs "Goldman Sachs"), [Lloyd Blankfein](/wiki/Lloyd_Blankfein "Lloyd Blankfein"), and graduated [Phi Beta Kappa](/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa "Phi Beta Kappa") with an [A.B.](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree, in [economics](/wiki/Economics "Economics") *[summa cum laude](/wiki/Summa_cum_laude "Summa cum laude")* in 1975. He received a [Ph.D.](/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") degree in economics from the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology") in 1979 after completing and defending his dissertation, *Long-Term Commitments, Dynamic Optimization, and the Business Cycle*. Schwimmer was born on November 2, 1966 (although some sources say November 12)[[4]](#cite_note-4), in [Flushing, Queens](/wiki/Flushing,_Queens "Flushing, Queens"),[[5]](#cite_note-newsday-5) [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), to attorneys Arthur (1941–2024) and Arlene Coleman-Schwimmer (born 1940).[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-hello-8) His family is [Jewish](/wiki/Jews "Jews").[[9]](#cite_note-9) He has a sister named Ellie (born 1965).[[10]](#cite_note-yahoo-10) His mother was a high profile divorce attorney who had represented several high profile figures including [Elizabeth Taylor](/wiki/Elizabeth_Taylor "Elizabeth Taylor") and [Rod Stewart](/wiki/Rod_Stewart "Rod Stewart"). His family subsequently moved to [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), where Schwimmer, at 10, had his first acting experience when he was cast as the fairy godmother in a Jewish version of *[Cinderella](/wiki/Cinderella "Cinderella")*.[[10]](#cite_note-yahoo-10) At the age of 12, Schwimmer went to a Shakespeare workshop given by English actor Sir [Ian McKellen](/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen") in Los Angeles.[[11]](#cite_note-guard-11) He recalls being riveted by the experience.[[11]](#cite_note-guard-11) Schwimmer then entered a contest in the Southern California Shakespeare Festival three years in a row, winning two first prizes.[[11]](#cite_note-guard-11)[[12]](#cite_note-f_word-12)

Following his mother's successful career as a divorce lawyer, the family moved to [Beverly Hills](/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), where Schwimmer attended [Beverly Hills High School](/wiki/Beverly_Hills_High_School "Beverly Hills High School").[[11]](#cite_note-guard-11)[[12]](#cite_note-f_word-12) His classmates included actor [Jonathan Silverman](/wiki/Jonathan_Silverman "Jonathan Silverman"). Garland has tended to favor deference to regulatory agencies.[[54]](#cite_note-54) For example, in *In re Aiken County* (2013), Garland dissented when the court issued [mandamus](/wiki/Mandamus "Mandamus") ordering the [Nuclear Regulatory Commission](/wiki/Nuclear_Regulatory_Commission "Nuclear Regulatory Commission") to process the [Yucca Mountain nuclear waste repository](/wiki/Yucca_Mountain_nuclear_waste_repository "Yucca Mountain nuclear waste repository") license.[[55]](#cite_note-55) In *[Americans for Safe Access v.
